chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Beware of the supplication of the oppressed, for it is raised above the clouds until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, looks at it, then He says: 'Raise it until I answer him.' And beware of the supplication of the father, for it is sharper than the sword.'
ai.seo_question: What makes the supplication of the oppressed and the father so powerful in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith underscores the metaphysical weight of divine justice by describing the oppressed's supplication as ascending above the clouds, a imagery reflecting the Quranic concept of Allah's direct attention to the wronged. The comparison of the father's supplication to a 'sharp sword' highlights its piercing efficacy, a nuance often discussed by Shia scholars to distinguish the unique spiritual authority of the patriarch within the family structure.
